headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest ctx-managed files and APIs, creating prompt-injection and data-flow risks; no direct evidence of a shared channel beyond filesystem/MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and supports MCP. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. No direct pairwise proof exists, so uncertainty is escalated to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ctx writes untrusted content into a shared workspace that gpt-researcher later reads
IF gpt-researcher ingests document text or MCP output as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Add provenance tags to files before handoff
Require a human review step before any prompt-like content is reused

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files and APIs, and gpt-researcher explicitly handles secrets plus broad network egress. ctx touches audit/runtime logs and MCP servers. If they share a workspace, sensitive material from ctx can flow into gpt-researcher outputs or third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default research workflows, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF ctx logs or graph data contain secrets or sensitive identifiers
IF gpt-researcher sends ingested file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Mount only read-only inputs into gpt-researcher
Redact logs before sharing them
Restrict outbound network access for research runs
Rotate any exposed API keys

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem access; gpt-researcher supports multiple instances, subprocesses, and broad network egress. Overlapping writes to shared files or artifacts can race without locking. The profiles do not show explicit coordination primitives, so conflict risk exists in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF multiple instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run one agent at a time for shared artifacts
Use immutable inputs and append-only outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe and organize tool events, while gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations. If ctx-generated summaries are fed into gpt-researcher without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into polished reports. No evidence shows a mandatory validation gate, so the interaction is risky but not clearly high.
conditions: IF ctx output is used as source material for gpt-researcher
IF no independent verification step checks citations or facts
mitigations: Require source-link verification before publication
Keep raw sources separate from generated summaries
Add a checklist for citation validation
Have a human spot-check final reports

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not show a clear residency or certification mismatch. gpt-researcher handles local documents and external APIs, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and MCP servers, but no specific regulated data class or jurisdictional conflict is documented. The other agent is cited because the compliance question is pairwise, but the evidence is weak.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF external APIs process data subject to a residency or retention rule
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings for both tools
Review API data-processing terms
Use a local-only mode for sensitive projects
